## The pipeline

```
tracker.api / create → tracker.scaffold → client drops into Shared/ → tracker.filer → tracker.scanner → tracker.reminder (on DRAFT_WEEKDAY) → a person sends the draft
```

- **`tracker/filer.py`** — Sorts the client's drop folder: moves each original into Shared/PBC/ untouched, copies a renamed working file into Prepared/... or 00 - Needs Review, and appends every move to _index.xlsx.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.filer`
  - constants: `INDEX_FILENAME` = '_index.xlsx', `INDEX_SHEET` = 'Index', `FILED` = 'Filed', `NEEDS_REVIEW` = 'Needs Review', `DUPLICATE` = 'Duplicate', `ASSIGNED_BY_PERSON` = 'assigned by a person'
  - imports: `tracker/locking.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/router.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`, `tracker/validators.py`

  - reads: `artifact:Shared/`, `artifact:_manifest.xlsx`
  - note: Content-hash de-duplication makes re-runs no-ops. Originals are moved byte for byte under their own names and never altered. Each drop is handled on its own: a drop that cannot be moved is left in place for the next run, a drop that fails after it was preserved is indexed as Needs Review with the error, and the index is written in a finally block so nothing moved into PBC/ is ever unrecorded. If Excel holds _index.xlsx, new rows wait in _index.pending.json and read_index() already sees them. Holds the engagement lock (tracker.locking) while it runs, so a sort and a scan never overlap. Files the client drops straight into the visible PBC/ are filed and indexed in place; a re-sent document whose working copy vanished from Prepared/ is re-filed rather than called a duplicate; a Document renamed in Excel keeps filing into the folder that already holds its files (assign_folders, not folder_name_for); empty client folders are cleared after sorting. assign_review_file() is the person's counterpart to file_drops(): moves the parked copy under the canonical name (or copies from PBC/ if it is gone), rewrites the index row as Filed with the ASSIGNED_BY_PERSON reason, learns a keyword onto the request, all under the engagement lock. INDEX_LAYOUT is the one description of _index.xlsx (header and width per IndexEntry field); the index is written and read back by header name, so a reordered column cannot shift a value.

  - constants: `UNMATCHED` = 'matched no request', `AMBIGUOUS` = 'matched more than one request', `EVIDENCE_CONTENT` = 'content', `EVIDENCE_FILENAME` = 'filename', `NO_REQUEST_ACCEPTS` = 'no request accepts .{extension} files', `CONTESTED_PREFIX` = 'looks like'

  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_filer.py`, `tests/test_rollover.py`
  - note: Extension alone never routes. A document matching one row's required keywords but failing its other rules is contested and blocks its own filing — misfiling a tax document is worse than not filing it. When nothing routes, the reason is the most useful one available: a document whose content fits a row that refused the file (size floor, type, unreadable PDF) is reported as CONTESTED_PREFIX, and a file every row refused for the same reason carries that reason. The filename fallback also accepts the run-together spelling (W2 for W-2) as a whole token. Eligibility is has_routing_rules(): keywords or a typed year; a year derived from Period only checks a document a keyword already matched.

  - constants: `SETTINGS_FILENAME` = 'settings.json', `KEY_CLIENTS_ROOT` = 'clients_root', `KEY_FIRM` = 'firm', `SET_ROOT_HINT` = 'python -m tracker.settings <folder>', `EXAMPLE_ROOT` = 'D:\\OneDrive\\Clients', `ENV_SETTINGS_DIR` = 'TRACKER_SETTINGS_DIR', `ENV_PRODUCT_NAME` = 'TRACKER_PRODUCT_NAME'

  - used by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/scheduling.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_settings.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: Replaced two roots (an env var for the app defaulting to a demo folder, a command-line path for the job) that nothing tied together. set_clients_root() refuses a folder that does not exist, so a typo cannot become an empty root the run walks for ever.
- **`tracker/templates.py`** — The per-form request catalog (FORM_TYPES, FORM_TEMPLATES): what each return type asks for and the keyword rules that recognise each document. The ONLY source of truth for the checklists; the wizard and the rollover read it directly.
  - constants: `FORM_LABEL_PATTERN` = 'Form {form}', `BASE_YEAR` = 2025, `PERIOD_PATTERN` = 'TY{year}', `YEAR_NOTE` = "Defaults to the most recently ended year; the checklist's periods follow it", `KEYWORD_DEFAULT_NOTE` = 'defaults to the document name'
  - imports: `tracker/manifest.py`
  - used by: `tracker/api.py`, `tracker/rollover.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_templates.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/samples.py`, `tests/test_api.py`, `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: item_from_spec() gives a rule-less request its own document name as the required keyword, because a request with no rule can never auto-file, and the safe extension default. default_tax_year() is the calendar's most recently ended year; template_items(form, year=...) shifts the catalog's base year to it, relative periods included. No date_pattern in the catalog: each row's Period implies its year check.
- **`tracker/validators.py`** — Tiers 1-2: does the file exist, is the extension allowed, is it big enough, is the PDF readable. Pure read-only functions plus passive cloud-placeholder detection for OneDrive and Google Drive.
  - CLI: `python -m tracker.validators`
  - constants: `OFFICE_LOCK_PREFIX` = '~$', `PDF_EXTENSION` = 'pdf'
  - imports: `tracker/__init__.py`, `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - used by: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/router.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
  - tested by: `tests/test_validators.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - note: Never downloads a cloud-only placeholder — a stub must never be filed as if it were the document. A file that vanishes between listing and stat is reported pending_sync, never raised — a scheduled scan must not die on one replaced file.

### tooling

- **`tools/repo_map.py`** — Builds and incrementally updates this map. Derives imports, exports, CLIs, test coverage and hashes from source; merges the curated layer on top.
  - CLI: `python -m tools.repo_map`
  - constants: `SCHEMA_VERSION` = 1, `MAP_INTRO` = 'Read this instead of re-scanning the repository.', `TESTED_BY` = 'tested by', `EXERCISED_BY` = 'exercised by', `NO_TEST_FILE` = 'no dedicated test file'
  - tested by: `tests/test_repo_map.py`
  - exercised by (imported, not its coverage): `tests/test_single_source.py`
  - reads: `docs/repo-map.curated.json`
  - note: Standard library only. `update` re-parses only files whose SHA-256 changed, and a change to this file forces a full rebuild — new derivation rules must not leave edges typed by the old ones. Test edges are three-way on purpose: `tests` (the test file owning the module by name) is coverage, `exercises` (any other test importing it) is not, and a test importing another test is a plain `imports`.

### ci

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — CI: runs the test suite and `repo_map.py check` on every push to main and every pull request.
  - reads: `requirements.txt`
  - note: The map check is the point. docs/repo-map.md is what agents read instead of re-scanning, its freshness is guarded by test_the_committed_map_is_current, and this workflow is what makes that guard run without anyone remembering to. Both steps always report, so a stale map and a failing test surface in the same run.

### desktop-app

- **`app/main.js`** — Electron main process. Spawns the Python API (`python -m tracker.api`, or the frozen executable package.json's config.apiName names in the portable build) and relays its JSON to the renderer over IPC.
  - imports: `app/package.json`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
  - note: This is the cross-language boundary: everything the UI can do is a tracker.api command.
- **`app/package.json`**
  - used by: `app/main.js`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
- **`app/preload.js`** — Context bridge exposing only the calls tests/test_single_source.py checks against main.js.call(args, payload), tracker.open(path) and tracker.pickFolder(). Nothing else crosses.
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
- **`app/renderer/app.js`** — The desktop UI: the form-type wizard, the request list and the scan results. Talks only to window.tracker from the preload bridge.
- **`app/renderer/index.html`** — Desktop app shell markup.
- **`app/renderer/logo.svg`**
- **`app/renderer/style.css`** — Desktop app styling.

### root

- **`Build App.bat`**
- **`Start App.bat`**
- **`api_entry.py`** — PyInstaller entry point. Freezes tracker.api into the executable app/package.json's config.apiName names, for the portable Windows app.
  - CLI: `python api_entry.py`
  - imports: `tracker/api.py`
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**
  - note: The only reason this exists is that PyInstaller needs a real script, not a -m module.
- **`conftest.py`** — Puts the repo root on sys.path so tests can `import tracker` without installing the package.
  - tested by: **no dedicated test file**

## Artifacts (files the system reads and writes at runtime)

- **`artifact:Prepared/`** — The firm-side working set: renamed copies sorted per request, plus 00 - Needs Review for anything that could not be identified. The client never sees this.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - read by: `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
- **`artifact:Shared/`** — The client's one drop folder — the only thing they see and the only thing they touch. Their originals end up in Shared/PBC/, still visible to them, untouched.
  - written by: `tracker/scaffold.py`
  - read by: `tracker/filer.py`
- **`artifact:_index.pending.json`** — Sidecar holding index rows for originals already moved into PBC/ that could not be written because Excel had _index.xlsx open. Read alongside the workbook and folded into the next successful write.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`
- **`artifact:_index.xlsx`** — Every original the client sent: where it came from, where it went, and what it was renamed to. The audit trail.
  - written by: `tracker/filer.py`
- **`artifact:_manifest.pending.json`** — Sidecar holding status updates that could not be written because Excel had the manifest locked. Merged into the next successful write.
  - written by: `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
- **`artifact:_manifest.xlsx`** — The engagement's request list and its live status, plus the Engagement sheet (client, link, due, sender, firm, reminders, active) the scheduled run reads. Sits OUTSIDE the client's shared scope — the accountant's file, not theirs.
  - written by: `tracker/manifest.py`, `tracker/scanner.py`
  - read by: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/registry.py`, `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/rollover.py`, `tracker/scaffold.py`
- **`artifact:reminder-draft.txt`** — The drafted chase email, waiting for a person to read, edit and send. Carries a fingerprint so the weekly job can tell whether it has been edited.
  - written by: `tracker/reminder.py`

## Rules that cut across the code

- **rule:no-AI-on-client-documents** — No generative AI ever reads a client financial document. Every routing and status decision comes from deterministic rules in the manifest.
  - enforced in: `tracker/content_check.py`, `tracker/validators.py`
- **rule:nothing-is-ever-sent** — Nothing is ever sent. The system drafts client emails and stops. There is no SMTP, no mail client and no network call in the reminder or scheduling path.
  - enforced in: `tracker/reminder.py`, `tracker/runner.py`, `tracker/scheduling.py`
- **rule:nothing-is-guessed** — Nothing is guessed. A document is filed only when exactly one request accepts it. Ambiguous, contested and unrecognized files go to 00 - Needs Review for a person - misfiling a tax document is worse than not filing it.
  - enforced in: `tracker/filer.py`, `tracker/router.py`
- **rule:originals-are-never-altered** — Originals are never altered. Files are moved byte for byte under their own names into Shared/PBC/; all work happens on copies, and every move is recorded in _index.xlsx.
  - enforced in: `tracker/filer.py`

## External dependencies

`child_process`, `electron`, `fs`, `openpyxl`, `path`, `pdfplumber`, `pypdf`, `pypdfium2`, `pytesseract`, `pytest`

## Updating this map

```
python tools/repo_map.py update    # after any code change (incremental)
python tools/repo_map.py check     # verify it matches the working tree
```

Derived facts (imports, exports, CLIs, tests, hashes) are parsed from the source — never hand-edit them. Descriptions, artifacts and cross-language hops are curated in `docs/repo-map.curated.json`; edit that file and re-run `update`.
